question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x-4,\, & 2\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot (2x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(2{x}^{2}-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot (2x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{43}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{43}{6}-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
